reference: Standalone Perl CLI (`perl`) is the independent oracle. In each parity script, system Bash selects `perl`; the candidate shell selects its embedded `bashperl` builtin. The suite requires the host `perl` command.
coverage: Perl expression evaluation and literal ARGV handling
multiple input files and ARGV naming
in-place edits, backup contents, and resulting fixture files
END block output and Perl exit status
syntax error status and diagnostics presence
fresh interpreter state and restoration of cwd, umask, and exported environment
exclusions: Perl system/exec and native XS behavior are deferred because they can affect process state beyond the fixture; no child process, signal, network, host path, credential, or privileged operation is exercised.
Interactive signal delivery and arbitrary file descriptor mutation require separately controlled process or syscall fixtures.

cases.purpose: Compare Perl expression evaluation and preservation of shell-significant argument bytes, including spaces, a literal command-substitution string, a glob, and an option-looking argument.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  bashperl -e 'my @n=(1..6); print join("|", @ARGV), ":", join(",", map { $_*$_ } @n), "\n"' -- 'a b' "'quote" '$(false)' '$HOME' '*' '-x'
else
  perl -e 'my @n=(1..6); print join("|", @ARGV), ":", join(",", map { $_*$_ } @n), "\n"' -- 'a b' "'quote" '$(false)' '$HOME' '*' '-x'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare -p processing and a per-record substitution over newline-terminated and unterminated input records.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  printf 'alpha\naardvark\nlast' | bashperl -pe 's/^a/A/'
else
  printf 'alpha\naardvark\nlast' | perl -pe 's/^a/A/'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare -n, -l, -a, and -F field splitting across multiple input records.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  printf 'ada:42\nbo:7\n' | bashperl -F: -alne 'print "$F[0]=$F[1]"'
else
  printf 'ada:42\nbo:7\n' | perl -F: -alne 'print "$F[0]=$F[1]"'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare Perl's NUL input-record separator with small deterministic binary input containing two separators and a final unterminated record.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  printf 'a\000b\000tail' | bashperl -0ne 'print uc'
else
  printf 'a\000b\000tail' | perl -0ne 'print uc'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare -n processing across two relative fixture files, including the current ARGV filename in output.
cases.script:
printf 'one\n1\n' > first
printf 'two\n2\n' > second
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  bashperl -ne 'print "$ARGV:$_"' first second
else
  perl -ne 'print "$ARGV:$_"' first second
fi

cases.purpose: Compare -i.bak edits inside the private fixture tree, including backup bytes and the modified file; the runner also compares modes and links.
cases.script:
printf 'one\n1\n' > file
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  bashperl -i.bak -pe 's/one/ONE/' file
else
  perl -i.bak -pe 's/one/ONE/' file
fi
while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done < file
while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done < file.bak

cases.purpose: Compare output from normal execution and an END block when the Perl program exits with a nonzero status.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  bashperl -e 'print "before\n"; END { print "end\n" } exit 7'
else
  perl -e 'print "before\n"; END { print "end\n" } exit 7'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare compile-failure status and require a diagnostic without depending on Perl-version-specific wording.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  bashperl -e 'my $x = ;'
else
  perl -e 'my $x = ;'
fi

cases.purpose: Check the documented Bash builtin type and help text without invoking Perl code.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t bashperl)
[[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 1
doc=$(help bashperl)
[[ $doc == *'Run real Perl in the current shell process.'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'Each invocation has a fresh interpreter.'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin\nhelp describes the Perl CLI and fresh interpreter contract\n'
cases.stdout:
builtin
help describes the Perl CLI and fresh interpreter contract

cases.purpose: Check the documented fresh-interpreter guarantee across two builtin invocations in one Bash process.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  bashperl -e 'our $x=42; print "$x\n"'
  bashperl -e 'print defined $x ? "leaked\n" : "fresh\n"'
else
  perl -e 'our $x=42; print "$x\n"'
  perl -e 'print defined $x ? "leaked\n" : "fresh\n"'
fi

cases.purpose: Check documented cwd, umask, and exported-environment restoration after Perl changes those values and dies; the Perl-created directory remains a relative fixture artifact.
cases.script:
export BP_KEEP=before
before=$PWD
umask 022
if [[ $(type -t bashperl) == builtin ]]; then
  if bashperl -e 'mkdir "sub" or die $!; chdir "sub" or die $!; umask 0077; $ENV{BP_KEEP}="changed"; $ENV{BP_NEW}="leak"; die "expected failure\n"'; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
else
  if perl -e 'mkdir "sub" or die $!; chdir "sub" or die $!; umask 0077; $ENV{BP_KEEP}="changed"; $ENV{BP_NEW}="leak"; die "expected failure\n"'; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
fi
mask=$(umask)
if [[ $status == 255 && $PWD == "$before" && $mask == 0022 && $BP_KEEP == before && ! -v BP_NEW && -d sub ]]; then
  printf 'cwd umask environment restored; fixture directory created\n'
else
  exit 1
fi
cases.stdout: cwd umask environment restored; fixture directory created

cases.purpose: Exercise Perl system/exec calls, signal handling, arbitrary descriptor changes, or native XS code that can affect the embedding Bash process.
cases.reason: A future disposable VM should provide a dedicated child-process fixture and syscall or XS mocks that record the requested process effects without launching host commands, signaling unrelated processes, changing host state, or loading an unreviewed extension.
